root.description: The id of the root the path is under

path.description: The routed file, relative to its root

anyOf.description: A content key: "<parserKind>.<keyKind>.<hex>" (keyKind sha256 | git-sha1 | git-sha256)

blob.description: The content key of the bytes, or null when the run holds none

variant.description: How the bytes were parsed, each under one fixed synthetic file name: `ts` (`.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, not a declaration file) as `vat.ts`, ScriptKind TS; `dts` (every name TypeScript's isDeclarationFileName accepts) as `vat.d.ts`, ScriptKind TS; `tsx` (`.tsx`) as `vat.tsx`, ScriptKind TSX; `js` (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`) as `vat.js`, ScriptKind JS

state.description: `facts`: the pair's rows are held; `defective`: the bytes or the file decide it (a parse error or another defect its instance's pair codes name, not text, a cap the bytes decide, a read the filesystem refused or failed), so the same file fails the same way every run: fix the file or exclude it in its instance's block (resources.extractors.data or resources.extractors.ts); `refused`: this run decided it (a time, heap or stack cap, a worker death, bytes changed or gone under the run, the machine out of descriptors or the path busy), so a rerun may answer, except a pair refused because a store-off run holds as many bytes of rows as it may: a rerun refuses it again, so run with the projection store on, inside a git repository

code.description: Why the pair is not `facts`, or null when it is

projection-ts--routes.description: A row of the derived `ts__routes` relation
